Headquartered in the Netherlands and operating globally, Doktar develops data-driven technologies that enable climate-smart and sustainable agriculture.
Our technologies, digital platforms, and sustainability advisory services help farmers, corporations, and governments improve productivity while protecting the planet.

The Opportunity

In this role, you will contribute to basin-scale water stress assessments, climate-risk analytics, groundwater and evapotranspiration analysis, and geospatial modelling workflows using satellite and climate datasets.
You’ll work on real-world environmental challenges by combining remote sensing, hydrology, geospatial analytics, and data science methodologies to support scalable and scientifically grounded decision-making systems.
This role is ideal for candidates who enjoy transforming complex earth observation datasets into interpretable and actionable insights.

What You’ll Do

Develop and maintain remote sensing workflows for water, climate, and agricultural analytics.
Work with satellite datasets such as Sentinel, Landsat, MODIS, GRACE, ERA5, and CHIRPS.
Support basin-scale analysis including evapotranspiration, water balance, drought, groundwater, and crop-water-stress assessments.
Process and analyze raster and vector geospatial datasets using Python and geospatial tools.
Build reproducible geospatial processing pipelines and automate analysis workflows.
Within the Data Science team, work across AI/ML, geospatial, and sustainability initiatives to convert environmental signals into practical insights for field operations and sustainability programs.
Support interpretation, visualization, and technical reporting of environmental and hydro-climatic analyses.
Contribute to methodology development for satellite-driven sustainability and water-risk assessments.

What We’re Looking For

5–7 years of experience in geospatial data science, remote sensing, Earth observation analytics, or GeoAI, ideally with exposure to agriculture, water, climate, or environmental applications.
Strong hands-on Python skills, with experience using scientific and geospatial libraries for data processing, analysis, and modelling.
Experience with Python-based geospatial and Earth observation workflows, including tools such as GeoPandas, Rasterio, Xarray/Rioxarray, GDAL, Google Earth Engine, and QGIS.
Solid understanding of raster and vector data processing, spatial analysis, map algebra, geospatial data pipelines, and reproducible analytical workflows.
Familiarity with satellite and climate datasets such as Sentinel, Landsat, MODIS, GRACE, ERA5, CHIRPS, or similar open Earth observation datasets.

Strong analytical thinking, scientific curiosity, and ownership mindset, with the ability to work on complex, real-world environmental problems in a collaborative Data Science team.

The Opportunity

Join Doktar, where we build satellite-driven data and analytics systems for agriculture, sustainability, and water security.
As a Senior Geospatial Data Engineer, you will design, build, and operate scalable geospatial data pipelines that transform large volumes of satellite, climate, and environmental data into reliable analytical products. You will work with datasets such as Sentinel, Landsat, MODIS, GRACE, ERA5, and CHIRPS to support basin-scale water assessments, climate-risk analytics, groundwater and evapotranspiration analysis, and agricultural intelligence.
This role combines geospatial engineering, Earth observation, and cloud-based data processing. You will collaborate with geospatial analysts, data scientists, machine learning engineers, and domain experts to take analytical methods from development into robust, reproducible, and production-ready workflows.
The role is well suited to someone who enjoys solving complex data-engineering problems and building dependable systems from large, heterogeneous Earth observation datasets.

Design, build, and maintain scalable pipelines for ingesting, processing, and serving satellite, climate, and environmental data.
Develop production-grade geospatial workflows for agricultural, water, climate, and sustainability applications.
Manage and continuously improve the CropMap geospatial database, ensuring its performance, scalability, reliability, and data integrity.
Process and manage large raster, vector, and time-series datasets using Python, SQL, and geospatial technologies.
Build reusable data-processing components and automate workflows for analyses such as evapotranspiration, water balance, drought, groundwater, and crop water stress.
Design efficient geospatial data models, storage structures, metadata standards, and data-access patterns.
Improve the performance, reliability, observability, and cost efficiency of geospatial processing workloads.
Implement testing, validation, versioning, monitoring, and quality-control mechanisms across geospatial data pipelines.
Operationalize methodologies developed by geospatial analysts, data scientists, and environmental specialists.
Develop services, APIs, and data products that make geospatial outputs accessible to downstream applications and analytical teams.
Establish engineering standards for reproducibility, documentation, code quality, and deployment.
Provide technical guidance through architecture decisions, code reviews, and mentoring of less-experienced team members.
Work across AI/ML, geospatial, product, and sustainability initiatives to convert environmental data into dependable operational insights.

What We’re Looking For

Typically 5+ years of relevant experience in geospatial data engineering, geospatial software engineering, Earth observation systems, or large-scale geospatial data processing, with demonstrated senior-level technical ownership.
Strong Python and SQL skills, with experience developing maintainable, tested, and production-ready data pipelines.
Advanced hands-on experience with PostgreSQL/PostGIS, including spatial database design, indexing, query optimization, and management of large geospatial datasets.
Strong experience with geospatial technologies such as GDAL, Rasterio, GeoPandas, Xarray/Rioxarray, QGIS, or Google Earth Engine.
Solid understanding of raster and vector processing, spatial databases, coordinate reference systems, map algebra, spatial indexing, and geospatial data quality.
Experience working with satellite and climate datasets such as Sentinel, Landsat, MODIS, GRACE, ERA5, CHIRPS, or comparable Earth observation sources.
Experience designing and operating cloud-based data workflows on Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud.
Hands-on knowledge of Docker, workflow orchestration, CI/CD, automated testing, and production monitoring.
Experience with scalable or distributed processing technologies such as Dask, Spark, Ray, or cloud-native geospatial processing frameworks.
Familiarity with modern geospatial formats and standards such as Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF, Zarr, GeoParquet, STAC, and spatial APIs.
Ability to optimize processing pipelines for performance, storage efficiency, reliability, and cloud cost.
Ability to translate analytical requirements into sound data architecture and production systems.
Clear technical communication skills, including architecture documentation, methodology notes, and stakeholder-facing explanations.
Strong ownership, analytical thinking, and the ability to make sound technical decisions in a collaborative environment.

Additional Advantages

Experience with agriculture, hydrology, water balance, evapotranspiration, drought, groundwater, sustainability, or climate-risk applications.
Experience operationalizing remote-sensing algorithms or machine-learning models.
Familiarity with Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, data catalogues, or geospatial API development.
Experience providing technical leadership, mentoring engineers, or defining engineering standards.

Detailed Job Description

PURPOSE

CST Canada Coal Limited (CST Coal) is seeking an Entry-Level Environmental Technologist to join our Resource Management Team. This position is responsible for performing field, laboratory and office functions which support delivery of the multi-faceted environmental program. The members of the Resource Management Team at CST Coal works together to remain compliant with all legislative and policy requirements governing its’ Approval to operate issued under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (EPEA).

About Us

The department of Resource Management at CST Coal is responsible for a variety of functions that contribute to mining coal safely and responsibly. We are a small department and the successful candidate will be able to participate in many different types of environmental work. Most importantly, CST Coal is committed to a safe work environment and creating a sustainable work-life balance. We provide excellent benefit coverage, RRSP matching, living allowance and a competitive wage. The beautiful views are just a bonus.

ACCOUNTABILITY

Reporting directly to the Superintendent of Resource Management, the successful candidate may be accountable for assisting contractors, consultants, casual labor, students and/or on-site logistics as required.

Responsibilities & Performance Standards

Reclamation

Assist with reclamation work which could involve supervising contractors, assessing soil depths, GIS data collection and tree planting/seeding.
Conduct reclamation monitoring on past reclamation.

Air Program (EPEA Section 4.2)

Completing Inspections of our continuous air monitoring equipment;
Collecting and processing data from the continuous air monitoring equipment;
Collecting samples and compiling data for report submission.

Mine Wastewater (EPEA Section 4.3)

Conduct inspections on ponds and other mine wastewater structures, and collect samples as needed.
Maintain and preform calibrations of all laboratory equipment.
Compiling and reviewing data for submission of monthly and annual reports
Assist with water management by supervising maintenance and planting wetland plants.
Responsible for ensuring adherence to established quality assurance and control of accepted laboratory practices.
Responsible for operating, organizing and maintaining field equipment.

Soil and Groundwater Monitoring (EPEA Section 4.6 and 4.7)

Participate in the inspection, collection and analysis of groundwater monitoring stations, as well as the processing and compiling of collected data.
Collect soil samples as required
Responsible for ensuring adherence to established quality assurance and control of accepted laboratory practices.
Responsible for operating, organizing and maintaining field equipment.

Additional Duties

Assisting other staff in the collection of field samples, data entry, reviewing and comparing site specific technical data, and researching applicable regulatory requirements.
Responsible for performing other related duties as required.

Qualifications

Education

A minimum two-year technical diploma in Environmental Science, Wildlife or Resource Management or related field is required.

Experience

This is an entry level position with a great opportunity to gain experience in many different environmental disciplines including water, air, wildlife, reclamation, waste management, and more. No prior environmental field experience working in an industrial, government or scientific community is necessary, however prior experience would be considered an asset. On the job training and feedback will be provided to help you be successful.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Safety first attitude
Solid writing and research abilities
Confident in a laboratory setting
Ability to operate or willingness to learn to operate all terrain and four wheel drive vehicles in a variety of environmental conditions
Love of the outdoors and adventurous spirit
Proficiency with the Microsoft Office Suite
Ability to work with minimal supervision
Knowledge of Alberta’s Flora and Fauna
Ability to use map & compass and GPS units/Avenza Maps
Excellent communication skills
Problem solving skills and ability to think quickly and be flexible
Maintain and Class 5 license and ability to maintain certificates for ATV, UTV and snowmobile

Physical Requirements

The selected candidate will need to be able to:

Handle loads over 20 kg. in weight
Regularly engage in physical exertion, i.e. shovel, lift and/or carry heavy materials
Concentrate for over 60 consecutive minutes
Work in environmental extremes for over 60 consecutive minutes
Sit for over 60 consecutive minutes
Listen for quiet sounds

WORK ENVIRONMENT

The successful candidate will be joining our team with CST and working on site at our Grande Cache Coal Mine. The commute from Grande Cache is approximately 20 km on Highway 40 North. Accommodations through CST Coal may be available or a monthly living allowance will be given to assist in finding your own accommodation.

The chosen candidate will be split between an office setting (approx. 30% of the time) and outdoors (approx. 70% of the time). Due to the nature of the mine site there is potential to be exposed to fire, wildlife, smoke, fumes, odors or chemicals associated with laboratory analysis and rough and steep terrain. Occasional travel may be required outside the work area in order to attend conferences, courses or meetings.

As a condition of employment, the incumbent is required to comply with pre and post-employment drug and alcohol testing as per the Drug and Alcohol Policy. As required, personal protective equipment will include the use of an approved hard hat, safety glasses, steel toe boots, hearing protection, CSA approved respiratory protection, protective clothing and gloves, personal flotation device, hip waders, goggles and ATV helmet. Vaccinations for rabies, hepatitis and tetanus are required.

Grande Cache, AB is located 180 km South of Grande Prairie and 145 km North of Hinton on Highway 40. In Grande Cache you will have access to a grocery store, post office, bank, hospital/doctor/dental offices, restaurants, shopping and more. Grande Cache is the perfect place for those who love nature and exploring the Rocky Mountains. Many locals enjoy their time of exploring the vast crown land around Grande Cache, the unique and rugged Willmore Wilderness Park and other local beauties including Pierre Grey’s Lakes Provincial Park and Sulphur Gates Provincial Park. In Grande Cache you will never run out of hiking trails, places to fish or camping spots

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About The Role

As a Drone System Validation Technician and Pilot
, you will be at the front line of our quality, safety, and reliability efforts. Your primary mission is to ensure that our defense-grade products meet rigorous operational standards before they are cleared for active duty.

Working within a dedicated flight testing team, you will manage, prepare, and operate fleets of newly assembled drones or related product during intensive field validation campaigns. By logging massive operating hours, you will actively hunt for rare, hard-to-replicate system bugs and edge-case anomalies. We are looking for operators who combine rigorous testing discipline with the hands-on piloting expertise required to accurately assess and validate nominal drone behavior in flight. Your technical feedback will directly enable our engineering teams to secure and polish our next-generation defense systems.

Responsibilities

Intensive Flight Testing: Conduct high-volume flight testing of newly assembled interceptors to log hours, validate systems, and actively hunt for rare, intermittent flight anomalies.
Aviation Performance Assessment: Manually operate, stress-test, and critically evaluate the flight dynamics of various platforms (multirotors, fixed-wing, flying wings, and RC planes) to ensure they handle exactly as designed.
Field Deployment: Lead and execute demanding on-site flight missions, sometimes lasting several weeks, under diverse weather and environmental conditions.
Mission Safety & Logs: Rigorously follow test checklists, maintain safety protocols during high-throughput flight operations, and accurately report flight observations to the engineering, production and industrialisation teams.

Candidate Requirements

Good RC/UAV Piloting Skills: You have extensive hands-on experience piloting RC planes, flying wings, or multirotor UAVs. Manual piloting dexterity and a deep instinct for flight mechanics are the absolute priorities for this role.
Rigor & Endurance: Strong discipline to run repetitive, structured test cycles with consistent attention to detail and unwavering focus on safety.
Adaptable Mindset: You thrive in fast-paced, lean startup environments where initiative, quick decision-making, and teamwork are valued over rigid hierarchy.
Field-Ready & Mobile: You possess a valid driver’s license (Permis B) and are ready to drive team vehicles, transport flight gear/drones. You are looking for a highly active, hands-on role where you will be out in the field on a daily basis, all year round.
Technical background: Any technical degree or professional experience in electronics, RC modeling, mechanics, or aeronautics is a great plus, but passionate self-taught pilots are highly encouraged to apply.

Certifications & FPV: Official drone pilot certifications, instructor ratings, or solid FPV (First Person View) racing/freestyle experience.
Military or Field Background: Past experience in specialized military units or demanding field-oriented professions.
Basic data/technical literacy: a basic grasp of autopilot systems, telemetry or flight-log reading, to help bridge the field and R&D. This is what turns an operator into a genuine validator, and is worth probing even if not required.

new_jobs.title: Lead UAV Systems
new_jobs.description:
IZI Ventures is the defence and strategic systems arm of the IZI group, headquartered in Bhopal. We design and build unmanned aerial systems for the Indian armed forces, paramilitary forces, and government agencies — with a technology core in GPS-denied navigation, jam-resistant communications, and autonomous flight. The group's established consumer electronics business provides manufacturing, supply chain, and financial depth; the defence vertical is our strategic growth engine, aligned with Aatmanirbhar Bharat.

The Role

The senior-most engineering position in our defence business — the technical authority for everything we build. You own the system architecture, the technical baseline, and the engineering organisation behind our lead platform: VANA, a GPS-denied-capable ISR multirotor in micro and small classes with tethered operation. You make the engineering calls — architecture, design freezes, vendor down-selects, make/buy — and you are accountable for taking VANA from development through flight test to a successful demonstration before a defence end-user evaluation. The founder sets direction; the engineering organisation, its decisions, and its output are yours. This is a builder's role: the team, the test discipline, and the first fielded-quality system are yours to create.

What You Will Own

- System architecture and technical baseline: airframe/propulsion trade-offs, avionics and flight control stack, GPS-denied navigation integration, EW-resilient datalinks, payload and tether subsystems, GCS software — with requirements, configuration control, and design freezes decided on evidence, on deadline
- Engineering decisions: authority over vendor/component down-selects (sensors, payloads, GNSS/INS, compute, propulsion), make/buy calls, and resource allocation — run through a decision-log discipline where nothing stays open past deadline
- Flight test and demonstration: test planning, data review, failure investigation, airworthiness sign-off — and a rehearsed, dated path to end-user evaluation
- Certification: DGCA UAS frameworks; DGQA/CEMILAC readiness and MIL-STD environmental/EMI-EMC expectations for military variants

Who We Are Looking For

- 4–8 years in UAV, aerospace, or defence systems engineering, with 3+ years leading multidisciplinary engineering teams — and still technically sharp: this is an engineering chair, not a coordination chair
- Hands-on depth in at least two of: flight controls and firmware (PX4/ArduPilot), avionics and sensor integration, airframe/propulsion design, embedded systems
- A demonstrated record of taking a complex aerospace or robotics system from development through flight test to delivery or induction — you have shipped and flown hardware, not only designed it
- Backgrounds we expect to fit: chief engineer / engineering leadership at HAL, ADE, or DRDO labs; senior engineering leadership at Indian UAV companies; or Armed Forces technical-branch officers with UAV development exposure
- A decision-maker by temperament: closes calls on incomplete information, on deadline, and owns the outcome
